text: Velma Springstead (22 August 1906 – 27 March 1927) was a Canadian track and field athlete born in Hamilton, Ontario. She won the gold medal in the high jump at the 1925 Canadian Track and Field Championships and became a member of the first women's track and field team of Canada to compete internationally. In July 1925, she participated in a track and field qualification at Varsity Stadium for the Amateur Athletic Union of Canada, which earned her a spot on that historic team. The following month, she finished third in the high jump and fourth in the hurdles at a track and field meet in London, England, where she was presented a trophy by Lord Decies for her courage. Outside of athletics, Springstead worked as a teacher at Calvin Presbyterian Church and as a secretary for Tuckett Tobacco Company. She died of pneumonia on 27 March 1927 in Hamilton, Ontario. After her death, the Velma Springstead Trophy was established to award the best Canadian sportswoman of the year, and in 2011, she was posthumously inducted into the Hamilton Sports Hall of Fame.
